record.title: Separation of survival and root-reinfection thresholds on strongly exponentially growing trees
record.statement:
Let $T$ be an infinite tree. Call a vertex $v$ **essential** if $T\setminus\{v\}$ has at least two infinite components. Say that $T$ has **strongly exponential growth** if there is some integer $r\geq1$ such that, for every $v\in T$, there are at least three essential vertices $w$ at graph distance $r$ from $v$. Let $\lambda_1$ be the survival threshold and let $\lambda_a$ be the threshold above which the root is reinfected at arbitrarily large times; together with $\lambda_b$, $\lambda_2$, and $\lambda_c$, these are the critical values defined for the contact process above. **Separation conjecture.** For any tree with strongly exponential growth, either all the above critical values are zero, or

$$
\lambda_1\neq\lambda_a.
$$

The claim concerns whether survival can begin strictly before recurrent reinfection of the root on sufficiently branching trees. The source gives no resolution.

record.title: Small-trade conjecture for subsets of Latin squares
record.statement:
Let $L$ be a Latin square of order $n\geq 3$, and let $S$ be a subset of its entries with $|S|\leq \left\lfloor n^2/4\right\rfloor$. For a Latin trade $T$ in $L$, let $R(T)$, $C(T)$, and $E(T)$ denote respectively the numbers of rows, columns, and elements involved in $T$. **Small-trade conjecture.** There exists a Latin trade $T\subseteq L$ such that

$$
T\cap S=\varnothing
$$

and at least one of $R(T)\leq 3$, $C(T)\leq 3$, or $E(T)\leq 3$ holds. This conjecture is motivated by the use of small trades to rule out small uniquely completable or critical sets. It is stated as a conjecture in the paper; no resolution beyond the discussion and the verified order-seven case is supplied here.

record.title: McCuaig–Ota conjecture on connected subgraph deletion
record.statement:
A graph $G$ is **3-connected** if deleting fewer than three vertices leaves it connected. For a subgraph $H$, write $G-V(H)$ for the graph obtained by deleting all vertices of $H$.

**McCuaig–Ota conjecture.** For every $ellgeq1$ there exists an $f(ell)$ such that every $3$-connected graph on at least $f(ell)$ vertices contains a connected subgraph $H$ on $ell$ vertices such that $G-V(H)$ is $2$-connected.

The conjecture is known for $ellleq4$ with sharp values of the threshold, but is wide open in general. Even the existence of a corresponding threshold for higher connectivity is not known.

record.title: The list-version of Thue's theorem for nonrepetitive sequences
record.statement: Let $n\geqslant 1$ and let $L_{1},\ldots,L_{n}$ be sets of symbols, each of size $3$. A sequence $s_{1}\ldots s_{n}$ is **chosen from lists** $L_{1},\ldots,L_{n}$ if $s_i\in L_i$ for every $i=1,\ldots,n$; it is nonrepetitive if it contains no adjacent repeated block. **The list-version of Thue's theorem.** For every $n\geqslant 1$ and every sequence of sets $L_{1},\ldots,L_{n}$, each of size $3$, there is a nonrepetitive sequence chosen from $L_{1},\ldots,L_{n}$. This is the list analogue of Thue's theorem that three symbols suffice for arbitrarily long nonrepetitive sequences; the paper's preceding argument establishes only that lists of size at least $4$ suffice, so the assertion for lists of size $3$ remains open.

record.title: The even-order non-separable subgraph conjecture
record.statement: Let $G$ be a non-separable graph of even order, meaning that no subset $W$ of its vertices with $2\leq |W|\leq |V(G)|-2$ becomes disconnected from its complement after any switching. record.title: The Big-Line-Big-Chromatic-Number Conjecture for planar visibility graphs
record.statement: Let $P$ be a finite set of points in the plane, and let $\mathcal{V}(P)$ be its visibility graph. A $(k-1)$-colouring assigns one of $k-1$ colours to each point. **Big-Line-Big-Chromatic-Number Conjecture.** For all integers $k\geq2$ and $\ell\geq1$ there is an integer $n$ such that if $P$ has at least $n$ points and is assigned one of $k-1$ colours, then $P$ contains $\ell$ collinear points or some visible pair receives the same colour; equivalently, $\chi(\mathcal{V}(P))\geq k$. record.title: The Stability Conjecture for generic relator tuples in free groups
record.statement:
Fix $k\ge 2$ and $m\ge 1$, and let $F=F(a_1,\dots,a_k)$ be the free group of rank $k$. For an $m$-tuple $\sigma$ of elements of $F$, write $R(\sigma)$ for the corresponding set of relators. **The Stability Conjecture.** There exists an algorithmically recognizable generic class $\mathcal{Y}$ of $m$-tuples of elements of $F$ such that, whenever $\sigma,\tau\in\mathcal{Y}$ and $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(F)$ satisfy that $R(\sigma)$ and $R(\alpha(\tau))$ have the same normal closure in $F$, one has

$$
R(\sigma)=R(\alpha(\tau)).
$$

The conjecture would extend the paper's rigidity arguments from generic quotients of the modular group to generic quotients of free groups of arbitrary finite rank. The authors report that their computer experiments support it, but no proof or resolution is given here.

record.title: The Wide Partition Conjecture
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid. An $M$-tableau of shape $\lambda$ is a Young diagram of shape $\lambda$ with an element of $M$ in each cell. A partition $\lambda$ **satisfies Rota's conjecture** if, for every matroid $M$ and every sequence $(I_i)$ of independent sets of $M$ with $|I_i|=\lambda_i$ for all $i$, there is an $M$-tableau $T$ of shape $\lambda$ such that the elements in row $i$ are exactly $I_i$ and the elements in column $j$ form an independent set of $M$.

**The Wide Partition Conjecture.** A partition $\lambda$ satisfies Rota's conjecture if and only if it is wide.

The conjecture generalizes Rota's basis conjecture and was formulated as a possible route to proving it by induction. The paper explains that necessity is straightforward, while sufficiency is the substantive unresolved direction; the free-matroid case is treated separately.

record.title: Conjecture PC5 on hereditary maximum parsimony trees
record.statement: Let $S:=f_1f_2\ldots f_n$ be a sequence of characters (an alignment) on a set $X$ of taxa, with $|X|=m$, and let $\mathcal{T}$ be a maximum parsimony tree for $S$. record.title: The minimum vertex-degree conjecture for perfect matchings in uniform hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $r\geq 3$ be an integer. An **$r$-uniform hypergraph** $H$ is a hypergraph whose edges have size $r$, and its **minimum vertex degree** $\delta_1(H)$ is the minimum number of edges containing any vertex. A **perfect matching** is a collection of pairwise disjoint edges covering all vertices.

**Minimum vertex-degree conjecture.** For each integer $r\geq 3$ there exists an integer $n_0=n_0(r)$ such that the following holds. Suppose that $H$ is an $r$-uniform hypergraph whose order $n\geq n_0$ is divisible by $r$. If

$$
\delta_1(H)>\binom{n-1}{r-1}-\binom{(r-1)n/r}{r-1},
$$
\nthen $H$ has a perfect matching.

The conjecture generalizes the paper's exact result for $3$-uniform hypergraphs and is motivated by the extremal construction in which the edges are precisely those meeting a smaller vertex class. Partial results were known from work of Hàn, Person and Schacht and of Markström and Ruciński; the general case is left open in the source.

record.title: The deck characterization of switching equivalence
record.statement:
Let $X_1$ and $X_2$ be graphs on $n$ vertices, and let $\mathcal{D}(X_i)$ denote the deck of vertex-deleted subgraphs of $X_i$. The decks are **switching equivalent** when there is a bijection between their cards that maps each card to a switching-equivalent graph. **The deck characterization conjecture.** The graphs $X_1$ and $X_2$ are switching equivalent if and only if

$$
\mathcal{D}(X_1) \sim \mathcal{D}(X_2).
$$

This is presented as an equivalent reformulation of the switching-equivalent reconstruction conjecture and is computationally verified in the supplied source for representatives with $4\leq n\leq 10$ vertices; the general statement is left open.

record.title: Stable-degree conjecture for permutation representations
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, let $\rho$ be a permutation representation of $G$, and let $P(\rho)$ be its permutation polytope. Set

$$
d:={\rm dim \,} P(\rho).
$$

Two permutation representations are stably equivalent when they differ by the stabilization relation used in the paper.

**Stable-degree conjecture.** There exists a stably equivalent permutation representation $\rho'\colon G\to S_n$ such that

$$

record.title: Symmetry-group conjecture for graphs of type $3_n$
record.statement:

record.title: The good-vertex conjecture for the independent-set bound
record.statement:
For a graph $G$, let ${\rm ind}(G)$ be its number of independent sets, let $d(u)$ be the degree of $u$, let ${\rm iso}(G)$ be the number of isolated vertices, and define

$$
\Pi(G)=2^{{\rm iso}(G)}\prod_{uv\in E(G)}\left(2^{d(u)}+2^{d(v)}-1\right)^\frac{1}{d(u)d(v)}.
$$

A vertex $x\in V(G)$ is **good** for $G$ if

$$
\Pi(G)\geq \Pi(G-x)+\Pi(G-x-N(x)),
$$

where $N(x)$ is the set of neighbours of $x$. **Good-vertex conjecture.** For every graph $G$ with at least one vertex, there is a vertex $x\in V(G)$ that is good for $G$. This conjecture would imply Kahn's independent-set bound.

319940.title: Sun's base- expansion conjectures
319940.literal_statement:
Let $n,m,k$ be positive integers with $m\geq 2$. For a positive integer, its base-$m$ expansion is the representation using digits from $0$ through $m-1$; a **non-zero digit** is a digit in this expansion that is not $0$.

**Sun's conjecture.** (I) There are at least $k$ non-zero digits in the base-$m$ expansion of

$$
\frac{m^k-1}{m-1}n.
$$

(II) The sum of all digits in the base-$m$ expansion of

$$
(m^k-1)n
$$
\nis at least $k(m-1)$.

These assertions generalize Sun's results for binary expansions and for prime bases, giving digit-expansion lower bounds for products involving geometric sums and $m^k-1$.

For $n\geq 1$, let ${\mathcal T}^0_n$ be the class of objects defined in the paper, let $D(\sigma)\subseteq\{1,2,\dots,n-1\}$ denote the descent set of $\sigma\in{\mathcal T}^0_n$, let ${\mathcal S}_n$ be the symmetric group, and let $A_n(x)$ be the $n$-th Eulerian polynomial.

**Eulerian descent-set distribution conjecture.** For any $n$ and any subset $D\subseteq\{1,2,\dots,n-1\}$,

$$
|\{\sigma\in{\mathcal T}^0_n\,:\,D(\sigma)=D\}|=|\{\pi\in{\mathcal S}_n\,:\,D(\pi)=D\}|.
$$

In particular,

$$
\sum_{\sigma\in{\mathcal T}^0_n}x^{\operatorname{des}(\sigma)+1}=A_n(x).
$$

The conjecture arose from experimental evidence and was checked by computer for $n$ up to $9$; the asserted distribution beyond those computations remains open.

318983.title: Lemke–Kleitman conjecture on indices of sequences over cyclic groups
318983.literal_statement:
Let $Z_n$ be the cyclic group of $n$ elements, let $d$ and $n$ be positive integers with $d\mid n$, and let $S$ be a sequence of $n$ elements in $Z_n$. For a subsequence $T$ of $S$, write $\sigma(|mT|_n)$ for the sum of the least positive representatives of the terms of $mT$, where $m$ is coprime to $n$. **Lemke–Kleitman conjecture.** There should exist a nonempty subsequence $T$ of $S$ and an integer $m$ coprime to $n$ such that

$$
d\mid\sigma(|mT|_n)\mid n.
$$

The case $d=n$ asserts that every sequence of $n$ elements in $Z_n$ contains a subsequence of index $n$. The paper states that this conjecture is false in general, giving counterexamples for $n=4k+2\geq22$, although related assertions hold under repetition hypotheses and are believed in some prime-order cases.

319242.title: General bias-forcing conjecture for oriented even cycles
319242.literal_statement:
Let $D$ be an oriented graph, let $n$ be its number of vertices, and let $e(D)$ be its number of arcs. For subsets $A,B\subseteq V(D)$, write $e(A,B)$ for the number of arcs from $A$ to $B$, and define

$$
bias(D):=\max\left\{e(A,B): A,B\subseteq V(D),\ e(B,A)\leq \frac{e(A,B)}{2}\right\}.
$$

**Even-cycle bias conjecture.** For each integer $k\geq 2$, there exists a constant $\varepsilon>0$ such that every oriented graph $D$ satisfying

$$
bias(D)<\varepsilon\frac{e(D)^{k/(k-1)}}{n^{2/(k-1)}}
$$

contains an oriented cycle of length $2k$.

This generalizes the paper’s proposed six-cycle bound and connects small orientation bias with the forced presence of longer even directed cycles. The source gives no indication that the conjecture is solved.

364497.title: Tverberg–Vrećica conjecture
364497.literal_statement:
Let $0 \le k < d$ be integers, and let $r_0, \dots, r_k$ be positive integers. Suppose that $P_0, \dots, P_k$ are sets of points in $\mathds{R}^d$ satisfying

$$
|P_i|=(r_i-1)(d-k+1)+1
$$

for each $i$. **Tverberg–Vrećica conjecture.** There exists a $k$-dimensional flat $V\subseteq\mathds{R}^d$ and, for each $i$, a partition of $P_i$ into $r_i$ parts such that the convex hull of every part of every partition intersects $V$. This conjecture generalizes the central transversal theorem in the same way that Tverberg's theorem generalizes Rado's centerpoint theorem. Its topological and colorful generalizations are known when all $r_i$ are powers of the same prime $p$ and $p(d-k)=p\cdot\operatorname{codim}_{\mathds{R}}V$ is even; it remains open otherwise.

318003.title: Bialostocki's zero-sum permutation conjecture
318003.literal_statement:
Let $n$ be a positive even integer, and let $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ and $w_1,\ldots,w_n$ be zero-sum sequences with terms in $\mathbb{Z}_n=\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$. Thus

$$
\sum_{k=1}^n a_k=\sum_{k=1}^n w_k=0.
$$

**Bialostocki's conjecture.** There exists a permutation $\sigma\in S_n$ such that

$$
\sum_{k=1}^n w_k a_{\sigma(k)}=0,
$$

where $S_n$ is the symmetric group on $\\{1,\ldots,n\\}$. The conjecture concerns pairing two zero-sum sequences so that their weighted inner product vanishes modulo $n$; the paper confirms it when the weights form an arithmetic progression with even common difference.

381393.title: De Pierro's conjecture on underrelaxed projection limits
381393.literal_statement:
Let $X$ be a real Hilbert space and let $C_1,\ldots,C_N$ be nonempty closed convex subsets of $X$, with metric projections $P_{C_i}$. For $\lambda\in]0,1]$, define

$$
Q_{\lambda}:=((1-\lambda)Id+\lambda P_{C_N})\cdots((1-\lambda)Id+\lambda P_{C_2})((1-\lambda)Id+\lambda P_{C_1}).
$$

Assume that $F_{\lambda}:=\operatorname*{Fix}Q_{\lambda}\neq\emptyset$ for every $\lambda\in]0,1]$. For $x\in X$, let

$$
x_{\lambda}=\operatorname*{weak}\lim_{n\rightarrow+\infty}Q_{\lambda}^{n}(x).
$$

Let $\mathcal{L}$ be the set of least-squares solutions,

$$
\mathcal{L}:=\left\{x\in X\mid \sum_{i=1}^{N}\left\Vert x-P_{C_i}(x)\right\Vert^2=\inf_{y\in X}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\left\Vert y-P_{C_i}(y)\right\Vert^2\right\}.
$$

**De Pierro's conjecture.** The weak limits satisfy

$$
\lim_{\lambda\rightarrow0^{+}}x_{\lambda}=P_{\mathcal{L}}(x).
$$

The conjecture concerns the behavior, as the underrelaxation parameter tends to zero, of weak limits generated by cyclic compositions of underrelaxed projections for inconsistent convex feasibility problems. It is false in general: a system of three compact convex sets in $\mathbb{R}^{3}$ provides a counterexample.

$$
\Delta(H_1)=p,\qquad \Delta(H_2)=q.
$$

Let $G\leq S_n$ be a permutation group, let $H\leq G$ be a subgroup, and let $P(G)$ and $P(H)$ denote the associated permutation polytopes. For a partition

$$
[n]:=\{1,\ldots,n\}=\bigsqcup_i I_i,
$$

write

$$
\operatorname{stab}(G;(I_i)_i):=\{\sigma\in G:\sigma(I_i)=I_i\text{ for all }i\}\leq G.
$$

**Stabilizer characterization conjecture.** If $P(H)\preceq P(G)$ is a face, then

$$
H=\operatorname{stab}(G;(I_i)_i)
$$

for some partition $[n]=\bigsqcup_i I_i$.

The paper notes that stabilizers of partitions provide an obvious class of subgroups whose permutation polytopes are faces. The conjecture asks whether every subgroup yielding a face arises this way; its resolution is not given.
